steps.text: Gather all ingredients. Line an 8-inch square pan with aluminum foil; set aside.
Combine sugar, marshmallow cream, evaporated milk, butter, and salt together in a large saucepan over medium heat; bring to a full boil and cook for 5 minutes, stirring constantly.
Remove from heat and add milk chocolate chips and semisweet chocolate chips; stir until chocolate is melted and mixture is smooth. Stir in nuts and vanilla.
Pour into prepared pan; chill in refrigerator for 2 hours, or until firm.

raw_recipe.headline: Aunt Teen's Creamy Chocolate Fudge
raw_recipe.description: The best fudge recipes are those that have been passed down through the family! Add your favorite nuts to this chocolate fudge for a delicious treat.

review.reviewBody: ***PLEASE READ IF YOU ARE HAVING TROUBLE WITH CRUMBLY, GREASY FUDGE!*** I've used this recipe probably 50 times, and I've had it not turn out twice. The first time I used generic marshmallow cream. I don't recommend using any store brand ingredients in this fudge. The second time I used an enameled cast iron french oven, and it didn't turn out that time, either. Every time I use my calphalon, it turns out great. Also.....work fast! The faster the better. Don't start timing until the mixture is at a full, rolling boil and then reduce the temperature slightly so that it doesn't scorch. Stir the entire five minutes and have the chocolate chips measured out ahead of time so you can dump them in as soon as you turn off the heat and stir like mad. Get the chips fully incorporated and pour immediately. It never fails!

Absolutely incredible fudge! It is perfectly smooth, creamy, chocolately, and all-around enjoyable. Try putting the marshmallow creme in the microwave for about 15 seconds before adding it to the pan; it will come out of the jar much easier. Though the cooking experience would have been less stressful with one, a candy thermometer really isn't necessary. One tablespoon of butter is just the right amount, and boiling the mixture for around 7 minutes instead of five can assure that the fudge will solidify. Some found that the recipe was a bit too sweet, so taking out 1/4 cup of sugar can tame some of the super-sweetness. Finally, using 2 cups of the semisweet chips and 1 cup of the milk chocolate chips instead of the other way around can make an even richer fudge (especially for those dark chocolate lovers like me). It is THE BEST fudge recipe around, and I am sure that I will make it again and again for years to come.

This was my first time to make fudge and it turned out great! Many people at my dessert buffet said that it was the best fudge they had ever had. It was so creamy - not grainy at all. I have to say, though, that I messed up the first time I tried it. Because I had the marshmallow creme in the very bottom of the pan and I got the heat too high too fast, I burned the marshmallow creme into hard brown chunks! The second time, I kept the temperature at low until it was mixed up well and then I turned the heat up to medium and boiled it. That worked like a charm.

Basically, this represents a terrific, 5-star fudge recipe; I would tweak the instructions, though. First, cook for 6-1/2 minutes, because at 5 minutes, it really needs to be kept in the fridge to maintain the right texture. If you DO prefer the super-creaminess of the 5-minute cooking time, then it will be far less "melty" if, after refrigeration, you cut it into squares and let the squares "air-harden" on racks or trays until the sides are not tacky. (Obviously, this is kind of a pain, so I go with the 6-1/2 minutes!) And finally: This is too much butter. 1 tablespoon works well, and the butter can actually be left out completely if you like.

Chocoholics Beware! This stuff is highly addictive! Sinfully rich, decadent, and creamy are just a few of the words that come to mind when describing this fudge. It's so good and so easy to make. I did cut the sugar back by 1/4 cup and used a non-stick pan which I highly recommend. Bring this to a boill slowly, stir constantly and you should have no problems. I lined my 8x8 pan with Reynolds non-stick foil and it came out perfect. This recipe is a definite keeper!

I stuck to recipe and it was wonderful! My only suggestion: ALWAYS put nuts in the oven for a quick roast/toast before putting them in sweets. Toasting the walnuts before putting them in the fudge released a warmer nutty flavor and crisped the walnuts so that it made the fudge even more amazing, and offset some of the sweetness.

I put the nuts in a pie plate and put them in 300 oven for 20 minutes, or until very fragrant. Don't let them go all the way to black, but a nice dark brown is ok.

Thank you for sharing this recipe. Done right it is wonderful -- smooth and creamy. Frankly, I screwed it up the first time and it came out dense, grainy and crumbling. I think I cooked it for too long as I didn't start counting the "boil" until it was fully bubbling. I also think I used a pan that was too big for cooking the mixture. Due to the great reviews, I tried again and used a few of the tips from the other reviewers to see if I could get a better result. These are the things I did differently: 1) used a smaller pan; 2) used 3 T of butter (and I probably could have reduced further); 3) added a couple more Tablespoons of the evaporated milk to the recipe (to make it creamier); 4) doubled the vanilla to 2 t; 5) started timing the boil earlier in the process and only boiled 5 minutes; 6) waited to add the marshmallow cream until AFTER the boiling process; 7) used more semi-sweet chocolate to develop a deeper chocolate taste (I used 2 1/2 cups of semi-sweet and 1/2 cup of milk chocolate) and I melted it in the microwave first. The result was rich creamy fudge. I think the main things which caused the different result included the smaller pan, shorter boiling time (not over boiling) and adding the marshmallow cream later in the process.

I have made this recipe for the past ten years. It never fails and people always ask for it. Every time I try someone else's, I say to myself, not as good as the one I make. You have to wait to start timing for five minutes as soon as it comes to a rolling boil, stir constantly, don't use generic marshmallow creme, and have your chips and nuts etc ready to mix in right away. I use a full bag of Ghirardelli milk chocolate and half a bag of Ghirardelli semi sweet chips, they are much better than the cheaper ones. It's THE best fudge I have ever made or tasted.

I made a batch of this in the past and at that time I thought it was good, but I forgot to review. 
This time around I made some changes, as my sweet tooth has changed. I guess old age does that?
The changes I made: Only used 1 cup sugar instead of 1 1/2 cup and added 1 cup frozen little marshmallows at the very end before folding into the prepped pan. I have been looking for a Rocky road fudge & couldn’t find one that suited me. So I altered this recipe as I knew I had liked it before altering it. 

These changes did not alter the texture, its creamy & melts in your mouth.
Followed directions exactly and the fudge turned out crumbly and hard. The recipe needs a temperature for the ingredients to be boiled to, to hopefully give everyone consistent results.

As a decades-long fan of Fantasy Fudge, I can definitively confirm that it has met its match with Aunt Teen's Creamy Chocolate Fudge!!This recipe is extremely delicious and very similar in taste to See’s Chocolate butter (and if you use Guittard brand chocolate chips, I dare say it will be exactly the same, as this recipe is VERY similar to See’s copycat recipes that I’ve seen on other websites).Please do wait the full two hours for the fudge to setup in the refrigerator. I didn’t wait long enough and some pieces toward the middle fell apart. Cut it into small squares as this fudge is extremely rich and a little goes a long way. I’m very pleased with this recipe. The long 5 minute boil ensures no graininess (when stirring and transferring the fudge into the 8”x8” pan, make sure you use CLEAN utensils free of ANY unmelted grains of sugar, because a single grain of sugar could nucleate a crystalline cascade that will make your fudge grainy!!). I did not deviate from this recipe, and it came out PERFECT. It’s not too sweet. In fact, it uses HALF the sugar and 1/3 the butter of Fantasy fudge. This will be my go-to recipe for Fudge from now on (in fact I may use it as the basis for our own Chocolate Pecan Eggs for Easter this year, because See’s prices are so dear).
Delicious, smooth , creamy and glossy. Every body loves it and when they ask for the recipe, I explain that its a well kept family secret .😁
My husband described it as "ridiculous" (meaning that he loved it). Sorry, Grandma, but this will be my fudge recipe going forward.

Super easy! My first time making fudge and it was really tasty! Gave the recipe out to a few friends, my mom and auntie. Thank you :) *** Followed the advice of not using store brand, used Jut-Puffed and Carnation for the milk and fluff***
Awesome & Super easy!
This turned out great! Everyone loved it at multiple parties and it’s easy!! I used about 7 candy canes and just used chocolate chips.
I have been making this fudge for years , the friend and family ask for it every holiday season. It is a real crowd pleaser.

This is my first time making fudge, but I’ve now used this recipe 3x and each time came out perfectly. I made the original chocolate, but then also tweaked it slightly to make 2 other flavors: - egg nog fudge (swap chocolate chips out for white chocolate chips, 2 tsp vanilla bean paste, 1 tsp ground nutmeg) - white chocolate mocha (swap chocolate chips out for white chocolate, 1 tbsp instant espresso powder, 2 tsp vanilla bean paste) I have ingredients to make one more batch and I’m excited to have such a great base to play around with flavors. This will definitely be my go-to recipe.

I have made it in the past without fail but I find it very very sweet. I am thinking about bypassing the sugar and evaporated milk and just using a lesser portion of sweetened condensed milk, and instead of milk chocolate I am going to go with Ghirardelli's 60% cacao dark chocolate chips mixed 50/50 with Ghirardelli's semi sweet.

I have been looking for an easy, creamy fudge without the use of a candy thermometer. THIS IS IT!!! It came out perfect, even when I doubled the batch. Made a second batch using just milk chocolate-and I have now found my perfect fudge recipe!
